metadata.licensing_note: Ibn Kathir died in 774 AH / 1373 CE, roughly six centuries before this text was digitised, so the work itself is out of copyright. The value 'cleared' is the one internal/ingestion.SourceRegistry.IsUsable compares against; the descriptive basis is recorded here because docs/rag-architecture-part1.md §6 words this field as 'public domain / licensed / pending rights clearance', which is a different vocabulary from the one the gate uses.
metadata.digitisation: third-party; the text is a quran.com API response, not a scan of a physical printing
known_caveats: Ayah 1 opens with the surah preamble (تفسير سورة يوسف) and Ibn Kathir's hadith on teaching Surat Yusuf, so it is matn-as-surah commentary rather than word-by-word exegesis of the verse.
Entry lengths vary from 88 to 9830 characters; the long entries on 12:3 and 12:106 carry long chains of narration that will need paragraph-level chunking rather than one chunk per ayah.
Citations and Quranic quotations appear inline in square and round brackets; they were kept in the text because Part 1 §7 treats footnotes as structure rather than noise.
metadata.verification_note: unverified by design (issue #3). Human spot-check of the text against a printed edition has not happened yet, so the source is unusable by retrieval until a reviewer sets verification_status to verified.
